title: Microsoft Copilot Dashboard: export de-identified user-level Copilot metrics
summary: The briefing's rollout dates, licence prerequisites, default state and export controls are supported by Microsoft's sources. It correctly reports the licensing discrepancy and the analyst exception; minor corrections would make the control routes and checklist-to-table coverage clearer.

claims.quote: This enables users to export row-level Copilot metrics from the Copilot Dashboard for reporting and deeper analysis.

claims.quote: The VFAM control is a single unified control for both the week-level and day-level export options.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn calls the export setting User-level export and insights.
claims.quote: The Export setting that previously controlled access to the export feature is now called User-level export and insights

claims.claim: The setting also governs user-level insights on specific cards.
claims.quote: This setting now controls access to the following: ... User-level insights on specific cards in the application

claims.claim: The setting also governs user-level insights from Interactive insights.
claims.quote: This setting now controls access to the following: ... User-level insights from Interactive insights

claims.claim: Turning the setting off removes more than downloads for leaders and managers.
claims.quote: When off, leaders and managers can't export user-level data or view user-level insights on specific cards, and Interactive insights provides aggregated insights only.

claims.claim: The analyst role retains user-level data access and its setting cannot be changed.
claims.quote: Since analysts already have access to user-level data through advanced analysis experiences, the above-mentioned setting is always on for the analyst role and can't be changed.

claims.claim: Export policy changes can take up to 24 hours to appear.
claims.quote: Changes can take up to 24 hours to appear in the web app.

claims.claim: The export policy is configured through Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Access setting, with the note directing selection of Viva Insights and Copilot Metrics Export.
claims.quote: Select Create a policy. ... Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. ... Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off
claims.fix: Make the app and feature selection currently given in the note explicit in the route: 'Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Viva Insights > Copilot Metrics Export > Access setting'. Keep the existing note that Learn calls the setting User-level export and insights.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId <FeatureId from Get-VivaModuleFeature> -Name <policy name> -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone creates the tenant-wide disabling policy.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone ... The FeatureId value is returned in the output of the cmdlet.

claims.claim: The web app policy uses Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Access setting, with the note directing selection of the Viva Insights web app feature.
claims.quote: Select Create a policy. ... Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. ... Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off
claims.fix: Make the app and feature selection currently given in the note explicit in the route: 'Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Viva Insights > Viva Insights web app > Access setting'.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId VivaInsights, FeatureId 'Viva Insights web app', IsFeatureEnabled $false and Everyone disables the web app tenant-wide.
